title: How Much Rent Can You Really Afford? (The Real Number)

lines.say: How much rent can you actually afford?
The popular rules give you a number. It's usually too high.
Let's compare the rules with the real number, using our example from episode one.

scene.label: Our example salary
scene.sub: after taxes and benefits: $1,850 every two weeks

lines.cap: Our example earns $60,000 a year. After taxes and benefits, that's $1,850 every two weeks.
lines.say: Our example earns sixty thousand a year. After taxes and benefits, that's eighteen fifty every two weeks.

scene.label: Landlord rule: income = 3× rent
scene.sub: the most a landlord would approve

lines.cap: Landlords often want your gross income to be 3× the rent. $5,000 a month, divided by 3: $1,667.
lines.say: Landlords often want your gross income to be three times the rent. Five thousand a month, divided by three. Sixteen sixty-seven.
The famous thirty percent rule. Thirty percent of five thousand. Fifteen hundred.

scene.text: The rules use gross pay. Rent comes out of take-home.

lines.say: Here's the problem. Both rules use your gross income. But you pay rent from take-home pay.
So let's work backwards, from what actually lands in your account.

lines.cap: Start with two paychecks: $3,700. Minus other bills, $1,071. Minus groceries and gas, $640. Minus surprise funds, $132. Minus fun money, $200. Minus 10% for goals, $370.
lines.say: Start with two paychecks, thirty-seven hundred. Minus the other bills, ten seventy-one. Minus groceries and gas, six forty. Minus surprise funds, one thirty-two. Minus fun money, two hundred. Minus ten percent for goals, three seventy.

lines.cap: What's left is your real rent number: $1,287.
lines.say: What's left is your real rent number. Twelve eighty-seven.

lines.cap: Side by side: the landlord rule says $1,667. 30% says $1,500. The real number is $1,287.
lines.say: Side by side. The landlord rule says sixteen sixty-seven. Thirty percent says fifteen hundred. The real number is twelve eighty-seven.

scene.label: Rent at the 30% rule ($1,500)
scene.sub: a month left for debt, savings, everything

lines.cap: Rent at $1,500 leaves just $157 a month for every goal you have.
lines.say: Rent at fifteen hundred leaves just a hundred fifty-seven a month for every goal you have.
And at the landlord's number, you'd come up ten dollars short. Every month.

scene.text: Our example pays $1,300: right at the edge.

lines.cap: Our example pays $1,300, just over the line. Which is why episode one had to work so hard to find money.
lines.say: Our example pays thirteen hundred, just over the line. Which is why episode one had to work so hard to find money.
If your rent is over your real number, you have options.

scene.head: IF RENT IS OVER YOUR NUMBER
items: Add a roommate or rent out a room
Negotiate at renewal, or move at lease end
Raise income: the number moves with it

lines.say: Add a roommate. Negotiate at renewal, or move when the lease ends. Cut a different fixed bill. Or raise your income, because the real number moves with it.
